scenes.heading: Baudhayana Sulba Sutra & Sacred Geometry
bullets: Composed between 800 and 500 BCE by Baudhayana and Apastamba
Foundational Sanskrit texts on geometric construction using measuring cords
Constructed exact Vedic fire altars with precise ratios and symmetry
scenes.narration: Composed between 800 and 500 BCE by Baudhayana and Apastamba, the Sulba Sutras are foundational Sanskrit texts on geometric construction using measuring cords. Using a taut rope and two wooden pegs, ancient geometers drafted exact right angles and circles on the earth without modern compasses.
scenes.visual_hint: Geometric Vedic altar proportions constructed with sacred measuring cord (Rajju) and pegs

scenes.heading: Baudhayana Diagonal Theorem
bullets: Pre-Pythagorean statement of the diagonal theorem
The rope along the diagonal of a rectangle produces an area equal to both sides squared
Applied to square and rectangular sacrificial altars
scenes.narration: Baudhayana explicitly stated the diagonal theorem: the rope stretched along the diagonal of a rectangle produces an area equal to the sum of both sides squared. Long before Pythagoras, Indian mathematicians described this exact right-triangle relationship.
scenes.visual_hint: Visual proof of Baudhayana diagonal theorem a^2 + b^2 = c^2 with geometric square subdivisions

checkpoint.q: Which Sulba Sutra explicitly formulated the diagonal theorem for rectangles?

scenes.heading: Rational Approximation of Square Root of Two
bullets: Derived to solve the problem of doubling a square altar area
Calculates 1.4142156, accurate to five decimal places
scenes.narration: To double the area of a square altar, the Sulba Sutras derived a remarkably accurate rational approximation for the square root of two to five decimal places. Adding one plus one third plus one twelfth minus one over four hundred and eight gave builders one point four one four two one five six.
scenes.visual_hint: Geometric construction of square doubling with fractional series approximation for sqrt(2)

checkpoint.q: What mathematical constant did the Sulba Sutras approximate to 5 decimal places?

scenes.heading: Area-Preserving Geometric Transformations
bullets: Methods for transforming squares into circles of equivalent area
Squaring the circle and circling the square
Preserving total sacred altar volume and surface area
scenes.narration: The texts also detailed area-preserving geometric transformations, converting squares into equivalent circles and trapezia for precise architectural symmetry. Like reshaping clay without changing its weight, Sulba geometry transformed square footprints into circular ones while keeping total area identical.
scenes.visual_hint: Area-preserving transformation morphing a square into an equal-area circle diagram

checkpoint.q: What was the purpose of area-preserving transformations in the Sulba Sutras?
options: Converting altars between square and circular shapes while keeping area constant
